set.prevailing_wage_basis: No program rule found. Labor Code 1720(b)(3) treats a public agency's transfer of an asset for less than fair market price as payment out of public funds, so a discounted sale of surplus land can trigger prevailing wage unless a 1720(c) exemption applies; Gov. Code 54233 is silent on wages. Outcome depends on sale price and project facts (https://california.public.law/codes/labor_code_section_1720).
set.audit_note: Tier 4 spot check 2026-11-08: Board item 25-1070 (Resolutions 25-200 to 25-204, adopted December 16, 2025) matches the parcel list; only 120 W. Fir St. is non-exempt surplus. The staff item itself does not mention approving an annual inventory. Prevailing wage changed from false (uncited) to unclear per Labor Code 1720(b)(3). Affordability note: 25% lower income applies to housing sponsors seeking SLA priority (Gov. Code 54222.5); if no agreement is reached and 10+ units are built, Gov. Code 54233 requires at least 15% lower income for 55 years rental or 45 years ownership.

reason: Material: prevailing_wage_trigger false is contradicted by Labor Code 1720(b)(3), which covers below-market transfers of public land, so it is set to unclear.
